newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 27.

text.p: There are four days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- APPLE DAILY said that with the handover almost here, the media only talked about how great the "one country, two systems" policy was, how wise the Communist Party was. But in reality, many people lacked confidence in the policy and were afraid that Hong Kong would become more like China. The paper urged Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa to carry out a proper election for the first Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) Legislative Council as soon as possible. If election is open, fair and democratic, many people would gain confidence towards "one country, two systems", it said

-- The Beijing-backed TA KUNG PAO said only when the central government effectively exercised power over Hong Kong's diplomacy and defence could the autonomy of the SAR be assured. The paper believed Hong Kong people would have a correct understanding of the relationship between the central government and the SAR government, between autonomy and sovereignty, and prevent some people from interfering in Hong Kong and China's internal affairs in the name of safeguarding freedom and democracy.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said the decisions of the U.S. and British governments to send officials to attend the swearing-in of the provisional legislature, together with the vote by the U.S. House of Representatives to uphold China's Most Favoured Nation trade status, showed that the two countries had adopted a more pragmatic attitude towards China. The paper said it would be good for Hong Kong, for U.S. business, and for Sino-US relations.
